transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what finally made me come in is that I just keep forgetting really basic adult things. Like... paying my bills, returning emails for job interviews, actually showing up for appointments, or just following through on regular errands. I recently graduated, and it's gotten to the point where this is starting to cost me real opportunities. I just can't seem to keep on top of it all.
Have you always had difficulty with organization and remembering tasks, or is this something that's become much worse recently?

It's always been this way, honestly. Um, even back in elementary school, my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was bright, but... I constantly lost my worksheets. I'd always rush through directions without really reading them, and, uh, I talked out of turn a lot. My desk was always so messy that I literally couldn't find my assignments when it was time to hand them in. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new problem for me, it's just having bigger consequences now.
When you're working on something that requires concentration, like reading an email or working on a project, do you find your mind wandering or do you have trouble staying focused on it?

Yeah, all the time. I'll sit down to do something important, like update my resume or work on a coding practice problem, and I just can't stay on it. 

If a text notification goes off, or if I hear someone talking outside... or honestly, even if I just have a random thought about another task I need to do, it pulls me completely off track. I just end up abandoning what I was doing, and usually, I don't even notice what happened until way later.
Do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, feeling restless, or having difficulty sitting still, even when you're supposed to be paying attention to something?

Yeah, definitely. Um, when I have to sit through an interview, or a meeting, or honestly even just a movie, I get this... this intense pressure inside my body. It feels like I just need to get up, or shift around in my seat, or do something with my hands. If I have to just sit perfectly still, I literally feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin.
When you think back to your childhood, before you were 12 years old, were you already showing these kinds of attention and restlessness problems, or did they start later?

I think I mentioned this a minute ago, but yeah, it was definitely happening before I was 12. Even in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was smart, but I was always losing my worksheets. I would just fly through the directions without really reading them, and I was always talking out of turn. My desk was a complete disaster, to the point where I couldn't even find my homework to turn it in. So, yes, it's been going on since I was really young.
Beyond the work and organization issues you mentioned, how has this affected your relationships with friends or family, or your ability to do well in school?

Well, it's definitely holding me back in a major way right now. Since getting fired, I've actually missed follow-ups for new interviews, which is just really frustrating. I even had to step back from a volunteer project that I really cared about because I just couldn't keep up with the responsibilities. So right now, I'm unemployed, and honestly, I just feel like I can't reliably manage the basic steps of moving my life forward. It's like I'm just stuck.

You mentioned losing your job and stepping back from volunteering. Looking back at your school years, did your attention and organization problems also affect your grades or your ability to complete school assignments?

Um, well... I know I mentioned losing my worksheets and having a messy desk when I was younger. So completing assignments was definitely always a struggle, mostly just because I couldn't find them or I'd rush through the directions. 

But as for my actual grades... I'm not really sure. I mean, I got my bachelor's degree, so I managed to pass my classes and get through it. I don't really have specific memories of my grades being terrible or failing things. I just know the day-to-day process of actually keeping track of the work was always really hard for me.
Do you find yourself interrupting people when they're talking, or acting on impulses without thinking through the consequences first?

Yeah, I definitely do that. In conversations, and even in interviews, I tend to jump in before the other person is actually done talking. I usually do it because I think I know exactly where they're going with their sentence, so I just start talking. 

But then, you know, I realize I completely cut them off, or I end up answering the wrong question entirely because I didn't actually wait to hear what they were asking. It's definitely something I struggle with.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with lifelong history of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity symptoms dating back to elementary school (before age 12), with clear functional impairment across multiple domains (academic, occupational, social). Symptoms include difficulty sustaining attention, distractibility by external stimuli and internal thoughts, restlessness/fidgeting, difficulty sitting still, interrupting others, and acting without deliberation. Recent job loss and inability to manage adult responsibilities represent significant current functional impairment. Symptoms are pervasive across contexts (school, work, interviews, social settings) and have been chronic since childhood. Diagnosis meets DSM-5 criteria for ADHD, combined presentation.
